reviewer: claude-opus-5-5 (agent), blind look at every hole in both modes

bro-hof-stadium-h02.reason: Lätt 3D: the trees in the lower right, beside the line of play, are bleached to a pale lime-white with glowing outlines, so they look overexposed and cut out next to the rest of the map.
bro-hof-stadium-h02.fault: Lätt 3D draws near broadleaf (birch) crowns pale lime with bright yellow cut edges in full sun; the same on builds before 27 November. The tree fragment shader in apps/golf/src/map/map-gl.mjs lights them too hot at close range.

bro-hof-stadium-h07.reason: Detaljerad 3D from the tee: a dark half-disc is cut off at the right edge of the view, and a thin dark spike stands up out of the water on the shoreline straight ahead of the tee.
bro-hof-stadium-h07.fault: The thin spike on the near shore is a procedural reed (ground-cover.mjs reedBlades) planted by main.js's reed scan, which gives every Bro Hof pond a Phragmites fringe where the 2025 photo shows a mown bank; fix the reed scan or opt Bro Hof out in scenery/bro-hof.js, then re-bake its scatter. The dark half-disc at the right edge is the asphalt cart path, as built.

bro-hof-stadium-h11.reason: Detaljerad 3D from the tee: several dark conical trees or posts stand up out of the open water to the left of the line, with no land under them.
bro-hof-stadium-h11.fault: The dark spikes in the water are procedural reeds, not trees: the reed scan (main.js, ground-cover.mjs reedWaterAt) counts a 6 m shore cell on both sides of the outline and Bro Hof's ponds were flown full, so reeds stand metres out in open water where the photo shows mown banks. Keep reeds on the bank side (or opt Bro Hof out) and re-bake.

bro-hof-stadium-h13.reason: Lätt 3D: the lake has a straight vertical cut along its left side, and a paler blue wedge with straight edges spills out below it into the land at the lower left.
bro-hof-stadium-h13.fault: Lätt 3D's shallow/deep water tone is read from a fixed mip of each tile's own mask (map-gl.mjs textureLod(uMask, vUv, 4.0)), so it jumps at tile edges and draws the straight cut and wedge; the lake itself is a curved U. Fix it in map-gl.mjs with a shore distance continuous across tiles.

bro-hof-stadium-h14.reason: Detaljerad 3D from above: the big lake in the lower left has a large milky white blotch in it that washes the water out, so it reads like haze rather than water.
bro-hof-stadium-h14.resolution: The milky patch is the sun's glint on Mälaren seen from above (water-shading.mjs, water-road.mjs): it sits where the reflected view meets the sun, its sharp side is a cloud shadow, and it moves with the camera; where the view faces away from the sun Mälaren is deep blue.

bro-hof-stadium-h15.reason: Lätt 3D: a paler blue wedge with straight edges sticks out of the lake into the land left of the fairway at the layup point, and in Detaljerad 3D from above a line of tree clumps floats in open water on the left of the lake with no land under it.
bro-hof-stadium-h15.fault: Two faults: the clumps stand on a real island in Mälaren that the water sheet and bed carve in main.js ignore (the outline's innerRings are not honoured), so the island and its trees are drawn under water; and the pale straight wedge in Lätt 3D is the per-tile water-tone fault in map-gl.mjs, as on Stadium 13.

bro-hof-stadium-h17.reason: Lätt 3D: the water around the island green has a lighter rectangle with a hard vertical seam just right of the green, so it reads as a square patch in the water.
bro-hof-stadium-h17.fault: The lighter rectangle round the island green is Lätt 3D's shallow/deep tone read from a fixed mip of each tile's own mask (map-gl.mjs), so tiles of different size meet at a straight seam; the pond has none. Fix it in map-gl.mjs with a shore distance continuous across tiles.

bro-hof-stadium-h18.reason: Detaljerad 3D from the tee: a lone bush stands on the fairway right on the aim line, and neither the top-down view, Lätt 3D nor the photo has a tree there.
bro-hof-stadium-h18.fault: The bush is a ground-cover scatter bush: main.js keeps bushes 24 m from the hole's line, which starts at the back tee, while the yellow and blue deck lies 41 m west of it, so the forward tees' line crosses rough. Widen the scatter's corridor to every tee's line in main.js, then re-bake.

bro-hof-castle-h02.reason: Lätt 3D: no bunker is drawn at the front left of the green, only its 123–129 m distance label, while the top-down view and the photo both show bunkers there.
bro-hof-castle-h02.fault: Both bunkers are drawn (map-paint.mjs), but the 123-129 m carry pill is centred on the bunker group (map-measure.mjs, map-overlay.mjs) and covers them at this zoom; set a hazard's pill beside its outline in map-overlay.mjs.

bro-hof-castle-h17.reason: Lätt 3D: the water to the right of the hole is covered in coarse white speckles that look like static, and in Detaljerad 3D from above a dark striped line cuts across the fairway at the right edge of the view.
bro-hof-castle-h17.resolution: The white speckles are Lätt 3D's sun glitter on the ripples (map-gl.mjs) in a view across the lake toward the sun, as on Stadium 13 and 15; the dark striped line is the driving range's artificial-turf mat strip with its bays (range-mat-line), on the range's grass west of the hole.

bro-hof-castle-h18.reason: Lätt 3D: the trees left of the line, from the tee up to about 200 m, are bleached to a pale lime-white with glowing outlines, unlike the deep greens on the rest of the course.
bro-hof-castle-h18.fault: Lätt 3D draws near broadleaf crowns pale lime-white with bright rims, the same on builds before 27 November: the trees are laser-placed and right, the fault is in the map's near-tree impostor drawing (map-gl.mjs TREE_FRAGMENT, atlases from tools/bake-map-trees.mjs).

bro-hof-stadium-h06.reason: I could not tell whether the wide pond across the front of the tee in Lätt 3D and in the from-tee view is the same water as the narrow creek with small ponds in the top-down view and the photo, because the top-down view and the photo strip are too small to compare.
bro-hof-stadium-h06.resolution: It is the same water: the creek runs through a chain of ponds, and the wide water before the yellow and blue tees is two of them (lm-water-659_64-27 and ortho-pond-stadium-06-north, open water with lily pads on the 2025 photo), wider from tee height than from above.

bro-hof-stadium-h05.reason: The photo is a thin, small strip, so I could not check the bunkers around the green that Lätt 3D draws against the photo.
bro-hof-stadium-h05.resolution: Stadium 5 has one bunker, left of the green (stadium-bunker-05-1); Lätt 3D draws it there and the photo strip shows it at its east end. The sand right of the green in Lätt 3D is Stadium 12's, also on the strip.

bro-hof-castle-h09.reason: I could not tell whether the bunkers the photo shows beside the green are left out of Lätt 3D or just fall outside its frame, because the green sits close to the top edge.
bro-hof-castle-h09.resolution: Lätt 3D draws both of Castle 9's greenside bunkers: they are the two small sand patches left of the flag just under the top edge; the other two are the fairway bunkers about 225-235 m out, labelled.

open.canonical-control-pending: No independent horizontal or RH 2000 ground control has been measured at Bro Hof; the frame is the 1 m national terrain and the 0.16 m orthophoto, which agree with each other.
open.canonical-frame: The ground origin is fixed in software and has not been approved against independent control, as at every other ground.
open.release-review: The fourteen-gate release review (phone timings, offline and rollback rehearsal) is not run; by the owner's decision of 27 November 2026 the course is released on this blind visual review of every hole in both modes instead.
open.surface-intake-pending: All 36 holes were traced on the 2025 orthophoto, looked at hole by hole and blind by the ring reviewer; by the owner's decision of 27 November 2026 no person reviews the outlines before release.
